acip: GNYIS PA NI, SPYIR NA BDAG CAG GI STON PAS, DMAN PA LA MOS PA THEG DMAN PA RNAMS LA CHAGS BRAL GYI SPYOD PA DANG , RGYA CHEN PO LA MOS PA PHAR PHYIN THEG PA PA BA RNAMS LA SA DANG PHA ROL TU PHYIN PA'I SPYOD PA DANG , ZAB MO LA LHAG PAR MOS PA GSANG SNGAGS RGYUD SDE BZHI'I GDUL BYA RNAMS LA 'DOD CHAGS KYI CHOS KYI SPYOD PA STE, SPYOD PA GSUM BSTAN PA LAS, SKABS 'DI'I SPYOD PA NI 'DOD CHAGS KYI SPYOD PA YIN LA,
wylie: gnyis pa ni, spyir na bdag cag gi ston pas, dman pa la mos pa theg dman pa rnams la chags bral gyi spyod pa dang , rgya chen po la mos pa phar phyin theg pa pa ba rnams la sa dang pha rol tu phyin pa'i spyod pa dang , zab mo la lhag par mos pa gsang sngags rgyud sde bzhi'i gdul bya rnams la 'dod chags kyi chos kyi spyod pa ste, spyod pa gsum bstan pa las, skabs 'di'i spyod pa ni 'dod chags kyi spyod pa yin la
english: This brings us then to our second point.  Generally speaking, our Teacher has taught three different modes of activity.  He taught the mode of activity which is free of desire to those of the lower way: to those who are attracted to something lower.  He then taught the mode of activity of the bodhisattva paths, and the perfections, to those of the way of the perfections: to those who are attracted to what is far-reaching.  And then He taught the mode of activity which utilizes desire to those of the four classes of the way of the secret word: to those who are deeply attracted to what is deep.  Of these three different modes of activity, the one we are talking about here is that where we utilize desire.
